title: How to add a watermark in Google Docs on Mac: step by step in your browser
metaTitle: How to add a watermark in Google Docs on Mac
description: How to add a watermark in Google Docs on Mac: Insert > Page elements > Watermark, text or image, then Done. Fixes for hidden watermarks included.
targetKeyword: how to add a watermark in google docs on mac
intro: To add a watermark in Google Docs on Mac, open the document in your browser and go to Insert > Page elements > Watermark. Choose Text or Image in the panel on the right, set it up, then click Done.
tldr: Open the document in your browser, then go to Insert > Page elements > Watermark.
In the panel on the right, choose Text or Image, set it up, then click Done.
Watermarks stay hidden in pageless format. Switch to Pages with File > Page setup.
Remove a watermark from the same panel with Remove watermark at the bottom.
Google Docs has no watermark shortcut. The Insert menu opens with ⌃⌥I.

blocks.text: Google's help pages describe Docs as a browser app. They do not describe a separate Mac app, so you work in a browser. The watermark steps are the same in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox, so use the browser you already have open. The Docs menus sit in a bar inside the page, below the browser's address bar. Look there first, not at the top of your screen.
Before you start on a Mac

Mac keyboards use Command (⌘), Option (⌥), Control (⌃) and Shift (⇧). Google's shortcut page lists the Insert and Format menus with Control and Option, not Command. Read each symbol before you press keys. One wrong modifier opens a different menu, or nothing at all. Windows habits can cost you a minute here.

Check your access first. If you can only view the file, ask the owner for editing access before you start. Then decide what the mark should say, and whether it should be words or a picture, before you open any menu. Changing your mind halfway costs more time than it saves.

A watermark covers the whole document. It repeats on every page and sits behind your text. One setting controls all pages. That is useful for a draft stamp, and it is a nuisance for a document with a few special pages.

Think about the reader before you pick a style. A word like DRAFT tells a reviewer the file is not final. A small logo reads as branding. Decide which message you want before you open the panel, because the mark will be on every page your reader sees.
Step by step: add a watermark in Google Docs

The steps below use the menu names from Google's help page for computers. Google does not publish a version number for the web app, so names can shift when Google updates the interface. If a name looks different on your screen, look for the same words in the same order.
Text or image watermark: which one to pick

Text works best for a single word or a short phrase, such as DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL or SAMPLE. Say you are sending a contract draft to a client. Type DRAFT in the text box, then read a page of body text. If the word fights with the sentences, adjust the panel options until it sits quietly behind them. Text is also quick to replace when the wording changes.

An image works better for a logo, a seal or a stamp. Click Image in the panel, then click Select image. You can pick a file from Google Drive, Google Photos, a web address, or your camera. You can also upload a file from your Mac. Choose a simple graphic with a clear shape. A busy photo competes with the words, and the reader loses both.

Long text is the usual mistake. A long phrase breaks up behind the body text and becomes hard to read. If you need more than a word or two, reconsider the wording. Shorter marks are easier to read and easier to replace later.
Remove or edit a watermark in Google Docs

To edit an image watermark, right-click it, then choose Select watermark. Click Image options in the toolbar. To edit a text watermark, right-click it, choose Select watermark, then click Edit watermark. On a Mac, Control-click works the same as a right-click. A two-finger click on a trackpad does too.
To remove a watermark, go back to Insert > Page elements > Watermark. Click Remove watermark at the bottom of the panel. Then scroll through a few pages to confirm the page is clean.

Say you inherit a file marked OLD VERSION, and the new draft should say DRAFT. Right-click the mark, choose Select watermark, then click Edit watermark. Change the words in the text box, click Done, and check the first page. You never have to add a second watermark on top of the first.
Why your Google Docs watermark is not showing

The most common cause is pageless format. Google hides watermarks in pageless view, along with headers, footers and page numbers. Those items come back when you switch to Pages. To switch, go to File > Page setup, select Pages, then click OK. The Format menu also has Switch to Pages format, which does the same job.
Switching to Pages brings the watermark back. You do not add it again. Check the layout before you share the file, so readers see the mark where you intended it.

Gaps in the watermark have a different cause. If parts of the mark disappear, the text may have a background color behind it. Select that text and remove its background color, and the whole watermark should show. Google's watermark page links to a separate help page for this step, so use it if the menu names differ.
Keyboard shortcuts for a watermark on Mac

Google's keyboard shortcut page lists no watermark shortcut. You need the mouse or trackpad for Insert > Page elements > Watermark. The fastest route is ⌃⌥I to open Insert, then Page elements, then Watermark. Some third-party guides say ⌘⌥I opens Insert on Mac. Google's page says ⌃⌥I, so trust that one and test it on your keyboard.

Other shortcuts help around the watermark. ⌘⌥F inserts a footnote. ⌘Enter inserts a page break. ⌃⌥O opens the Format menu, where you find Switch to Pages format. Use these to move faster around the watermark steps. The watermark itself still needs the menus.

Test the shortcut once before you rely on it. Press ⌃⌥I with the document open and see whether the Insert menu appears. If nothing happens, click Insert in the menu bar instead. The mouse path always gives you the same result.
Printing and offline work in Google Docs

Google's watermark help page does not say how a watermark prints. Some third-party sites report print problems, but Google does not confirm them. Before you print a full run, print one page or save a PDF. Then check that the mark sits where you expect.

Offline work needs more setup. Google's offline help says you need Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Private or incognito windows are not supported. Install the Google Docs Offline extension, then open Google Drive, go to Settings, and turn on Offline. Open Docs from there. Google's page does not say whether watermarks behave differently offline, so test one on a copy first.
Mistakes people make with watermarks

items: Adding a watermark in pageless view, then thinking the feature failed.
Choosing a busy image that makes the body text hard to read.
Searching for a watermark shortcut that Google does not list.
Trusting a shortcut from a random guide over Google's own keyboard page.
Forgetting to check the last page, where the mark sometimes looks different after edits.

blocks.text: Another mistake is editing the wrong object. Click the text, and you edit your words. Right-click the watermark itself, then choose Select watermark. That way the panel changes the mark, not the paragraph under it.
Sharing a watermarked document with a team

A watermark stays in the file when you share it. Anyone with access sees the mark, so decide who should see it before you send the link. If a colleague needs to comment on the text, ask them to leave comments rather than edit the mark. The guide on [adding a comment in Google Docs](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-google-docs) shows the browser steps.
What to do next in Google Docs

Watermarks often come with other page setup. You may need a header and footer, or page numbers, next. The guides on [adding a header and footer](/how-to/add-a-header-and-footer-in-google-docs) and [adding page numbers](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-google-docs) cover those steps. If you add footnotes to the same file, the [footnote guide](/how-to/insert-a-footnote-in-google-docs) explains the ⌘⌥F route.

If you want help while you work in Docs, the [Lazur page for Google Docs](/apps/google-docs) explains voice help, shortcuts and dictation in your browser. Lazur points at the control you need and explains it. It does not click for you, so the watermark steps stay yours to finish.
Google updates its menus from time to time. If a name in this guide no longer matches your screen, check Google's watermark help page first.

faq.question: Is there a Google Docs app for Mac that has a watermark menu?
faq.answer: Google's help pages describe Docs as a browser app. They do not describe a separate Mac app. Use Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox. The Insert menu and Watermark option work the same way in each.

faq.question: Does a watermark appear on every page?
faq.answer: Yes. Google's help page says watermarks repeat on every page and sit behind your text. If a page looks empty, check whether the document is in pageless format, because pageless view hides watermarks.

faq.question: Can I remove a watermark from one page only?
faq.answer: Google's watermark help describes removing the watermark through Remove watermark in the panel. It does not describe removing one page only. If one page needs no mark, consider keeping that page in a separate document.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to add a watermark?
faq.answer: No. Google's keyboard shortcut page lists no watermark shortcut. Press ⌃⌥I to open the Insert menu, then click Page elements and Watermark.

faq.question: Why do some guides say ⌘⌥I opens the Insert menu?
faq.answer: Some third-party sites claim ⌘⌥I opens Insert on Mac. Google's keyboard shortcut page says ⌃⌥I. Use Google's combination, and test it on your keyboard before you rely on it.

faq.question: Will the watermark print?
faq.answer: Google's help page does not say. Some third-party sites report print problems. Print one page or save a PDF first, and check the result before you print the full document.

faq.question: Can I add a watermark while I am offline?
faq.answer: Google's offline help covers editing with Chrome or Edge and the Google Docs Offline extension. It does not say whether watermarks behave differently offline. Test on a copy, in a normal window rather than a private one.

task: Add a watermark to a Google Doc on a Mac
appliesTo: Google Docs in a browser on macOS, Apple silicon and Intel Macs
requirements: A Mac with Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox installed
Edit access to the Google Doc you want to mark
A few minutes to test the watermark on one page

steps.name: Open the document in your browser
steps.text: Go to docs.google.com in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox, then open the file. Make sure you can edit it. The watermark steps are the same in each browser, so use the one already open.
steps.tip: If the file lives in Google Drive, open it from there and it opens in Docs.

steps.name: Open the Insert menu
steps.text: Click Insert in the Docs menu bar, below the browser's address bar. You can also press ⌃⌥I. Google's keyboard shortcut page lists that combination for the Insert menu on Mac.
steps.tip: Some guides say ⌘⌥I. Google's page says ⌃⌥I, so test that one first.

steps.name: Go to Page elements and choose Watermark
steps.text: Point at Page elements in the Insert menu, then click Watermark. The watermark panel opens on the right side of the window. Google's help page gives this same path for computers.

steps.name: Choose Text or Image
steps.text: In the panel on the right, click Text to type words, or click Image to use a picture. Pick one now. You can edit the watermark later from the same panel.

steps.name: Set up a text watermark
steps.text: Type the words into the text box in the panel. Then use the panel's formatting options to set how the text looks. Google's help page does not list every option, so check the panel on your screen.
steps.tip: Pick a short phrase. Long phrases are hard to read behind body text.

steps.name: Or set up an image watermark
steps.text: Click Select image. You can choose a file from Google Drive, Google Photos, a web address (URL), or your camera. You can also upload a file from your Mac.
steps.tip: A simple logo with a clear shape usually reads better behind text than a busy photo.

steps.name: Click Done
steps.text: Click Done at the bottom of the panel. The watermark appears behind your text and repeats on every page.
steps.tip: If nothing appears, check whether the document is in pageless format. The troubleshooting section explains the fix.

steps.name: Check a few pages
steps.text: Scroll through the document and look at the first page, a middle page and the last page. Confirm the watermark is visible and that the body text is still easy to read.

troubleshooting.problem: The watermark does not appear anywhere
troubleshooting.fix: Check the page format first. Go to File > Page setup, select Pages, and click OK. You can also use Format > Switch to Pages format. Then scroll to a few pages and look again.

troubleshooting.problem: The watermark has gaps or missing parts
troubleshooting.fix: The text behind the gap likely has a background color. Select that text, remove its background color, and check again. Google's help page links to separate steps for background color if your menus differ.

troubleshooting.problem: The watermark makes body text hard to read
troubleshooting.fix: Right-click the watermark and choose Select watermark. Then choose Edit watermark for text, or Image options for an image. Adjust the settings and check a page of body text, not just the first page.

troubleshooting.problem: The watermark did not show up on a printout
troubleshooting.fix: Google's help page does not cover printing. Some third-party sites report print problems. Print a single page or save a PDF, and check it before you print the full document.
